title: Replace prototype SystemScene with the pinned MIT YEIS native body, point, and orbit renderer

scope.subject: Product-grade system-scale rendering for Personal Universe using the existing YEIS native system model inside the shared React Three Fiber canvas

research_summary: Keep pinned MIT YEIS e520568 as the universe/system authority and React Three Fiber as the host. Reuse the YEIS BodyRenderer, BodyPoints, OrbitLines and only their required pinned-MIT closure instead of polishing the current project-owned schematic SystemScene. Keep Personal Signal content binding and the shared destination model outside the renderer adapter. Closure audit confirmed BodyRenderer imports pinned-MIT ProceduralShips.ts; it is therefore explicitly included before implementation rather than being retroactively admitted.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT YEIS already implements near-body rendering with body-specific meshes, rings, tile globes and scale-sensitive visibility.
Pinned MIT YEIS already implements distant body point rendering so the system remains legible before individual bodies are large enough for full meshes.
Pinned MIT YEIS already renders native orbital paths from StarSystem data and is the correct source of system-scale orbital geometry.

The pinned application composes OrbitLines, BodyRenderer and BodyPoints against one StarSystem and updates them from a floating-origin camera; this establishes the intended native subsystem orchestration.
Cosmos provides a broader universe-scale rendering stack, but adopting it for system view would create a second spatial engine next to the already-selected YEIS authority.
React Three Fiber exposes the existing Three scene, camera and renderer to narrow adapters, so a YEIS render subsystem can be hosted without another canvas.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep the selected pinned MIT YEIS full solution. Cosmos is capable but would duplicate universe ownership and navigation semantics.
Keep the existing R3F canvas and adapt native YEIS render objects to it instead of creating another render loop or canvas.
Reuse the pinned MIT YEIS BodyRenderer, BodyPoints and OrbitLines orchestration, plus only the required pinned-MIT closure.
The project already vendors much of the pinned YEIS shader closure. Reuse those assets and add only missing renderer support files rather than rebuilding orbital and body materials.

candidates.name: Pinned MIT YEIS native system renderer stack
candidates.source: YEIS MIT e520568 BodyRenderer + BodyPoints + OrbitLines
candidates.reason: It is already the selected universe authority, consumes the native StarSystem model directly, and covers mesh, point, orbit and scale transitions without a parallel system model.

candidates.name: Cosmos system renderer replacement
candidates.reason: Strong scale handling, but using it only for system view would split camera/spatial authority from YEIS and require model translation at every navigation boundary.

candidates.name: Existing React Three Fiber host
candidates.reason: Provides the current renderer, scene lifecycle and product integration surface; the YEIS subsystem should be adapted into it rather than replacing it.

coverage_matrix.capability: Native system bodies and orbital geometry
coverage_matrix.decision: Use pinned YEIS BodyRenderer and OrbitLines directly over the native StarSystem.

coverage_matrix.capability: Cross-scale body visibility and distant point representation
coverage_matrix.decision: Use pinned YEIS BodyPoints together with BodyRenderer instead of maintaining the schematic project-owned body markers.

coverage_matrix.capability: Preserve Personal Signal and destination authority
coverage_matrix.decision: System renderer accepts the already-resolved native system and reports picked body identity back through the existing destination adapter.

coverage_matrix.capability: Single WebGL host and mobile quality control
coverage_matrix.decision: Host the native render subsystem inside the current R3F canvas and retain existing quality-mode ownership.

decision.rationale: Replace only the prototype SystemScene presentation with the pinned MIT YEIS native system render subsystem, while keeping the current R3F host, destination model, content placement and product HUD. This gains the mature native body/orbit behavior without introducing a second universe engine.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: Cosmos is a viable broad renderer, but the project already selected YEIS as universe authority and has native StarSystem/body identities throughout navigation. Replacing only this layer with Cosmos would add translation and duplicate scale/camera ownership.

decision.fallback: If direct camera-unit adaptation proves too coupled, retain YEIS as the data/orbit authority and introduce only a narrow camera-relative scale adapter around the pinned renderer classes before considering any project-owned system renderer.
